title: How to Use Dictation on Mac (2026): Shortcuts and Commands
summary: How to turn on and use dictation on a Mac: the shortcut, voice commands, fixes, and when a dedicated app is worth it.
body_markdown:
Every Mac ships with dictation built in, and most people never turn it on. That is a shame, because it takes about a minute to set up, it costs nothing, and it works in nearly every app where you can type. This guide covers how to use dictation on a Mac from start to finish: switching it on, the keyboard shortcut, the spoken commands for punctuation and formatting, what to check when it misbehaves, and the point at which a dedicated dictation app starts to earn its price.


**The short answer:** to dictate on a Mac, open System Settings, click Keyboard, and turn on Dictation. Then click where you want text, press the Microphone key (or your Dictation shortcut, or choose Edit, then Start Dictation), and speak. Press Escape when you are done. Dictation also stops on its own after 30 seconds of silence.


The steps below follow Apple's current[Mac User Guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/use-dictation-mh40584/mac) , written for macOS 27 at the time of writing. The same System Settings path applies back to macOS Ventura. On older versions the app is called System Preferences and the layout differs.


## How to turn on dictation on a Mac


1. Choose the Apple menu, then **System Settings** .
2. Click **Keyboard** in the sidebar. You may need to scroll down to find it.
3. Go to the **Dictation** section and switch it on, then click **Enable** .
4. If your Mac asks whether you want to improve Siri and Dictation, choose **Share Audio Recordings** or **Not Now** . Either choice leaves Dictation working. You can change your mind later under Privacy & Security, in Analytics & Improvements.


That is the whole setup. While you are on that screen, look at three other settings in the same Dictation section, because they decide how pleasant this is to use:


- **Languages.** Click Edit to add every language you dictate in. With more than one, you can switch mid-dictation by clicking the language label next to the cursor.
- **Microphone source.** Automatic is fine for most people. If you use a headset or an external mic, select it here.
- **Shortcut.** This is the key you will press dozens of times a day, so pick one deliberately. More on that next.


## The Mac dictation shortcut


There are three ways to start dictating once it is enabled:


- **The Microphone key.** On recent Mac keyboards it sits in the function row, on F5. Press and release it to start Dictation. Pressing and holding the same key activates Siri instead, which is the most common reason people think dictation is broken.
- **Your Dictation keyboard shortcut.** In System Settings, under Keyboard, open the Shortcut pop-up menu in the Dictation section and choose one of the presets, such as pressing the Fn (Function) key twice.
- **The menu bar.** In most apps, choose Edit, then Start Dictation.


To set your own shortcut, choose **Customize** in that same Shortcut menu and press the keys you want. Apple's own example is Option-Z. A custom shortcut is worth having if your keyboard has no Microphone key, or if a double-press keeps colliding with another tool.


## How to dictate on a Mac, step by step


1. Click in any text field so the insertion point is where you want the words to go.
2. Press the Microphone key or your shortcut.
3. Wait for the cursor to highlight and pulse, or for the tone. That is the signal that your Mac is listening.
4. Speak at a normal pace and volume.
5. Press Escape, the Microphone key, or your shortcut again to stop.


A few behaviors are worth knowing:


- **There is no time limit while you are talking.** Apple says you can dictate text of any length without a timeout. Dictation only stops automatically when it hears no speech for 30 seconds.
- **You can type while you dictate.** On a Mac with Apple silicon, the keyboard keeps working during dictation. The cursor stops pulsing while you type and resumes when you stop, so you can fix a word by hand and keep talking.
- **Punctuation is mostly automatic.** In supported languages, Dictation inserts commas, periods, and question marks for you. If you would rather speak your own punctuation, turn off Auto-punctuation in the Dictation settings.
- **Uncertain words are underlined in blue.** If you get "flour" when you meant "flower," click the underlined word and pick the alternative, or retype or re-dictate it.


## Mac dictation commands


While you are dictating, certain spoken phrases are treated as instructions instead of text. These come from Apple's[list of dictation commands](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/commands-for-dictating-text-on-mac-mh40695/mac) , and they are always available while Dictation is active.


**Line breaks and spacing**


- "new line" is the same as pressing Return once
- "new paragraph" is the same as pressing Return twice
- "tab key" inserts a tab
- "no space on" and "no space off" run the words in between together with no spaces


**Punctuation**


- "period" (or "full stop"), "comma", "question mark", "exclamation mark"
- "colon", "semicolon", "ellipsis", "hyphen", "dash", "apostrophe"
- "quote" and "end quote"
- "open parenthesis" and "close parenthesis", with matching commands for square brackets, braces, and angle brackets


**Capitalization**


- "caps on" and "caps off" for title case
- "all caps" to capitalize the next word only
- "all caps on" and "all caps off" for a run of uppercase text


**Numbers and symbols**


- "numeral" before a number to get the digit, and "roman numeral" for the Roman form
- "at sign", "ampersand", "asterisk", "hashtag", "percent sign", "underscore", "forward slash", "backslash"
- "dollar sign", "euro sign", "pound sterling sign", "yen sign"
- "plus sign", "minus sign", "equal sign", "greater than sign", "less than sign"
- "copyright sign", "registered sign", "trademark sign"


**Emoji**


In supported languages you can say the name of an emoji followed by the word "emoji," for example "heart emoji" or "car emoji."


One detail that surprises people: a new line or new paragraph appears when you finish dictating, not the instant you say it.


## Does Mac dictation work offline, and is it private?


It depends on your Mac and your language, and Apple tells you which case applies to you. With Dictation enabled, open System Settings, click Keyboard, and read the text below the Dictation switch. It says whether your voice input for general text dictation (messages and notes, as opposed to dictating into a search box) is processed on your device or sent to Apple's servers. If yours is not processed on device, you need an internet connection to dictate.


Separately, sharing audio recordings with Apple to improve Siri and Dictation is opt-in. You chose during setup, and you can change it any time in Privacy & Security under Analytics & Improvements.


## Dictation versus Voice Control


macOS has a second voice feature that people often confuse with this one. **Dictation** turns speech into text. **Voice Control** , under Accessibility, lets you run the whole Mac by voice: clicking, scrolling, opening apps, and editing text with spoken commands. It was built for people who cannot or prefer not to use a keyboard and mouse.


The two do not run side by side. When Voice Control is on, Apple notes that you dictate through Voice Control and standard Dictation is not available. If your dictation shortcut suddenly does nothing, check whether Voice Control got switched on. Our[Mac dictation comparison](https://aquavoice.com/vs/mac-dictation) goes deeper on that split.


## If dictation is not working on your Mac


Apple's[troubleshooting page](https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/if-dictation-on-mac-doesnt-work-as-expected-mchlc480652b/mac) lists the checks that resolve most problems. Work through them in this order:


1. **Confirm Dictation is still on** in System Settings, under Keyboard.
2. **Check the shortcut.** Make sure you are pressing the one selected in the Shortcut menu, and that you are tapping the Microphone key instead of holding it.
3. **Check the language and region** in the Dictation languages list.
4. **Check the microphone.** Confirm the right device is selected as the Microphone source. For an external mic, open Sound settings, click Input, and raise the input volume.
5. **Check your connection.** If the text under the Dictation switch says your speech is not processed on device, dictation needs internet access.
6. **Reduce noise.** Background noise and echoey rooms hurt recognition. A headset microphone helps.
7. **Check Voice Control.** If it is on, standard Dictation is unavailable.


## How to turn off dictation on a Mac


Go back to System Settings, click Keyboard, and switch Dictation off. If the only problem is that you keep triggering it by accident, you do not have to disable it: change the Shortcut to something you will not press by mistake.


## Where built-in dictation runs out, and when to upgrade


Apple Dictation is a good tool and the right place to start. For short messages, quick notes, and replies, it may be all you ever need. The limits show up when dictation becomes how you do real work, and they are limits of scope, not of quality:


- **Names, jargon, and code.** Dictation is a general-purpose system, and standard Dictation has no vocabulary list you can edit to teach it your product names, clients, or technical terms (Voice Control has one, but that is a different mode).
- **Fixing mistakes.** In standard Dictation, corrections happen by hand: you click the underlined word, or retype it.
- **Long thinking pauses.** Thirty seconds of silence ends the session, so you restart it each time you stop to think.
- **It stays on Apple devices.** If you also write on a Windows PC, your setup does not come with you.


This is the gap dedicated dictation apps fill. We build[Aqua Voice](https://aquavoice.com/) , so read this part as informed rather than neutral, and judge the checkable claims for yourself.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the keyboard shortcut for dictation on a Mac?** Press the Microphone key in the function row (F5 on recent Mac keyboards), or use the shortcut selected in System Settings under Keyboard, in the Dictation section. The Shortcut menu there offers presets such as pressing the Fn key twice, plus a Customize option for your own key combination. You can also choose Edit, then Start Dictation in most apps.


**Why does dictation keep stopping on my Mac?** Dictation stops automatically when it detects no speech for 30 seconds, and it also stops if you press Escape, the Microphone key, or your shortcut. While you are speaking there is no time limit. If it stops mid-sentence, check your microphone input level and, if your Mac does not process dictation on device, your internet connection.


**Does Mac dictation work without the internet?** On some Macs and in some languages, yes. With Dictation enabled, the text below the Dictation switch in Keyboard settings tells you whether your speech is processed on your device. If it is not, dictation needs an internet connection.


**How do I add punctuation when dictating on a Mac?** In supported languages, Dictation adds commas, periods, and question marks automatically. You can also say the name of the mark, such as "comma," "exclamation mark," or "open parenthesis," and say "new line" or "new paragraph" for line breaks. To speak all punctuation yourself, turn off Auto-punctuation in the Dictation settings.


**Is there something more accurate than Apple Dictation for Mac?** For everyday messages Apple Dictation is often enough. For names, technical terms, and long-form writing, dedicated apps with tuned models and a custom dictionary are more accurate. In a 9to5Mac test on the same passage, Apple Dictation made 17 errors to Aqua Voice's 1. Our[Mac roundup](https://aquavoice.com/blog/best-ai-dictation-app-for-mac) compares the options.
